content: Do we happen to have a source for the claim that the process from Theorem 11.3 (in the blueprint) is a quasi-martingale?
We only want to state this equivalence for real-valued processes, don't we?
The equivalence is claimed here: https://almostsuremath.com/2012/04/12/quasimartingales/ (search for "Métivier" in the page)

Lemma 6 there says that the quantity Var that he uses to define quasimartingales is the same as what appears in Theorem 11.3 of the blueprint. And there is a sentence that claims that his definition is equivalent to the one of Métivier (but without proof).
Yes, that whole page is about real-valued processes. And our Theorem 11.3 is also about those processes.
Okay, thank you very much, I should be able to take it from here.

I don't know if it is useful in any way since we are following another source, but Métivier's proof of the existence of càdlàg modifications for quasimartingales is his Theorem 10.9 and corollary 10.10.
I don’t know. But the proof is easy in the real case.

And the
implication fails for infinite dimensions. So, my question was rather unnecessary, sorry for that.
